record.original_question: Let S denote the class of all separable metrizable spaces. A GO-space X is cleavable over S when, for each subset A of X, there is a continuous map f_A from X into a member of S that separates A from its complement, meaning f_A(x) is not equal to f_A(y) whenever x is in A and y is in X minus A. Characterize exactly which GO-spaces are cleavable over S without assuming restrictions on cardinal functions such as cellularity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A GO-space (generalized ordered space) is a triple $(X,\tau,<)$ where $<$ is a linear order on $X$ and $\tau$ is a Hausdorff topology on $X$ that has a base consisting of order-convex sets and is finer than (or equal to) the open-interval topology induced by $<$. Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote the class of all separable metrizable topological spaces. A topological space $X$ is said to be cleavable over $\mathcal{S}$ if for every subset $A\subseteq X$ there exist a space $Y_A\in\mathcal{S}$ and a continuous map $f_A:X\to Y_A$ such that $f_A(x)\neq f_A(y)$ whenever $x\in A$ and $y\in X\setminus A$.

Provide an intrinsic characterization of those GO-spaces $X$ that are cleavable over $\mathcal{S}$, without imposing any restriction on the cardinal functions of $X$ (such as cellularity, density, weight, etc.).
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results on cleavability of GO-spaces over separable metrizable spaces are known (e.g., Bennett–Byerly–Lutzer, "Cleavability in Ordered Spaces", Order 2001), giving characterizations under cardinal-function restrictions such as bounded cellularity. A full intrinsic characterization without such restrictions does not appear in the literature, and the problem is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Cleavability in Ordered Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes cleavability of GO-spaces over metrizable spaces and presents examples related to cleavability over separable metric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial characterizations of cleavability of GO-spaces over separable metrizable spaces are available, typically under cardinal-function restrictions.
